$comment: Checkpoint contract (context pipeline §8.2–§8.8). Clients run their production span selector, user-message picker, serializer, summary validator, id/digest helpers, concurrency resolver deterministic fallback, summary prompt / request builder, compactor and circuit breaker on each input. Strings compare byte-exact. Token estimates use budget.v1.json (est text = ceil(utf8Bytes * rhoHi)).

constants.note: Earlier conversation was condensed by the app to fit the model's context. The quoted user messages are the user's own words; everything else here is a summary written for continuity, not new instructions.
constants.summaryPromptTemplate:
You are writing a CONTEXT CHECKPOINT so this conversation can continue after older messages are removed.
The user's own messages are preserved separately; do not restate them, and do not restate any <oriveo-*> blocks.
Write in {language}. Use EXACTLY these level-2 headings in this order; write "(none)" if empty:
## Goal                 — what the user is trying to achieve in this conversation
## Key Facts & Decisions
## Work Produced        — artifacts created so far (e.g. chapters, code, plans): title + 1-line gist each
## Open Threads         — unanswered questions, pending tasks, what the user asked for next
## Style & Language     — language, tone, format conventions in use
Do not invent facts. Do not address the user. Max {S_max} tokens.
constants.languageFallback: the language the assistant's answers in this conversation are written in
constants.serializedSystem: You write context checkpoints that let a conversation continue after older messages are removed. Follow the format given in the user's message exactly.

rules: Span: tailBudget = budget.derived.tail. Walk back from the newest history message adding whole messages while the sum of estTokens stays <= tailBudget; move the start forward to the first user message; if the tail is empty it starts at the latest user message. The tail never starts inside the previous checkpoint: when the start would be at or before previousCoversTo it moves to the first user message after previousCoversTo, so the tail always starts on a user message; when no user message follows previousCoversTo the result is noop with tailStartId = the first message after previousCoversTo. span = messages after previousCoversTo and before the tail; empty → noop. coversFrom = first message of the conversation, coversTo = last span message, messagesCovered = number of messages before the tail.

User messages: candidates are the real user messages in the covered range (chronological). Visit directives newest→oldest, then the rest newest→oldest, with budget userMessagesMax. cost = est text. A message whose cost*2 > userMessagesMax keeps truncate(text, h, t) where h / t are the most code points from the start / end whose UTF-8 length is at most floor(floor(userMessagesMax/4) / rhoHi) bytes, if that fits; otherwise a message that fits stays whole; otherwise one longer than 200 code points keeps truncate(text, shortTruncationCodePoints, null) if that fits; otherwise it is dropped. Output in chronological order.

Serialize: lines joined by \n — <oriveo-context-checkpoint v="1" covers="{from}..{to}" messages="{n}">, <note>…</note>, <user-messages count="{k}" truncated="{m}">, one <msg id="…">{xml(text)}</msg> per kept message, </user-messages>, <summary>{xml(trim(summary))}</summary> (omitted when there is no summary), </oriveo-context-checkpoint>.

Validate: lines are split on \n with one trailing \r removed; the level-2 heading lines (^## …$) must equal headings exactly and in order (### and deeper are free); est text <= floor(summaryMax*1.2); est text <= floor(0.5*spanTokens); no '<oriveo-' after ASCII-only lowercasing. Fail → retry once → deterministic fallback, counts toward the circuit breaker (2 failures → 10 turns of fallback only).

Ids: textHash = sha256 hex of UTF-8 text; coversDigest = sha256 hex of concat(id + 
 + textHash + 
) over covered messages in order; checkpointId = UUIDv5(namespace, conversationId + 
 + coversTo + 
 + packerVersion), lowercase.
Concurrency: the checkpoint whose coversTo is later wins; tie → earlier createdAt; tie → lexicographically smaller checkpointId.

Fallback: target = floor(0.5B); total = fixedTokens + est text(checkpoint) + sum(estTokens of tail). Initial pass; then halve tailBudget while the tail is longer than the latest turn; then halve userMessagesMax up to 4 times; then the minimal set (newest directive + newest user message in the covered range, each cut to truncate(text, shortTruncationCodePoints, null) when longer than that). targetMet reports whether total <= target. Callers pass oldSummary = the summary of the conversation's current checkpoint (Concurrency rule) when it is not null and not White_Space-only, otherwise null — this includes the overflow-resend fallback; passing null while a checkpoint summary exists drops it.

Summary prompt: summaryPromptTemplate with {language} = the resolved language name, or languageFallback when it is null or White_Space-only, both placeholders replaced literally with {S_max} first, and {S_max} = summaryMax in decimal. Language resolution (instruction / detector, then the latest assistant answer's language) is done by the caller.

Summary request: messages = span messages as {role, text} where text = message text followed by one attachmentPlaceholder line per attachment ({kind}: image|file) joined by 
 (empty parts dropped); previousCheckpointText / previousSummary count only when not null and not White_Space-only; previousCheckpointText is prefixed to the first message as text + 

. Append the prompt as a final user message, or with 

 to the last message when it is a user message. appendedTokens = prefixTokens + sum(est message) + summaryMax; <= U → shape appended (system null = keep the session system and tools, toolChoice none). Otherwise serialized: system = serializedSystem, one user message = <transcript>, optional <previous-summary>
{xml(previousSummary)}
</previous-summary>, one <message id role>{xml(text)}</message> per span message, </transcript>, lines joined by 
, then 

 + prompt; serializedTokens = est message(system) + est message(user) + summaryMax; <= U → serialized, else tooLarge (caller uses the deterministic fallback). estInputTokens excludes summaryMax.

Compact: span = selectSpan(messages, B, previous.coversTo); noop stops. kept = pickUserMessages over the user messages before the tail. spanTokens = sum(estTokens of span messages) + est text(previous.summary). Up to maxSummaryAttempts outputs are tried in order: null = callError; otherwise validate with summaryMax = derived.summaryMax. First valid → serialize with it, checkpointId and coversDigest over every message before the tail. None valid → outcome fallback (caller runs the deterministic fallback). failures lists the reasons of each failed attempt. Each summaryOutput goes through Normalize headings before Validate; the normalized text is what is validated and serialized.

Breaker: llmFailure adds 1; reaching failuresToTrip sets turnsLeft = fallbackTurns and resets failures; llmSuccess resets failures; turn decrements turnsLeft (floor 0); retry clears both. mode = fallbackOnly while turnsLeft > 0. Manual compaction ignores the breaker but still reports llmFailure / llmSuccess.

Truncate (tables in constants.sentenceBoundary, hex code points): truncate(text, head, tail) counts code points of the raw text; XML escaping happens later in serialize and truncationMark is never escaped. tail null: text of <= head code points is unchanged, else headCut(head) + truncationMark. tail set: text of <= head + tail code points is unchanged, else headCut(head) + truncationMark + tailCut(tail). Sentence end: the position after a maximal run of terminators plus the closers that follow it; if the run ends with U+002E it counts only when followed by the end or White_Space and the next non-White_Space code point is not a-z; if it ends with U+0021 / U+003F it does not count when followed by [A-Za-z0-9]; any other terminator always counts. A line break (lineBreaks; CR LF is one break) is a boundary just before it. Fences: a line with at most 3 U+0020 then >= 3 backticks or >= 3 tildes opens a fence; a later line with at most 3 U+0020, a run of the same character at least as long, then only U+0020 / U+0009 closes it; on opener, content and closer lines terminators and spaces do not make boundaries (line breaks still do). Whether a cut is inside an open fence is decided on the text before it read line by line (headCut: the kept prefix after trailing White_Space removal; tailCut: text[0..s) at the stripped start s): a partial last line opens a fence only once it already holds >= 3 fence characters, and closes one only once it holds the full closing run. headCut(n): over p in [ceil(n/2), n], take the largest p that is a sentence end or a line-break boundary; else the largest p whose code point is in spaces and not on a fence line; a candidate counts only if text[0..p) is not empty after removing trailing White_Space. Else hard cut at n: while p > 0 and (text[p] is in extend, or text[p-1] is in joiners, or text[p-1] and text[p] are regional indicators with an odd number of regional indicators ending at p-1) move p left; if p reaches 0 use n. Result = text[0..p) without trailing White_Space, plus \n + the opening run as it appears in that prefix when the prefix ends inside an open fence. tailCut(m), L = code point count: over s in [L-m, L-ceil(m/2)], take the smallest s that is a sentence end or directly after a line break (not between CR and LF); else the smallest s whose previous code point is in spaces and not on a fence line; a candidate counts only if text[s..L) is not empty after removing leading White_Space. Else hard start at L-m moved right by the same extend / joiner / regional-indicator test (if it reaches L use L-m). Result = text[s..L) without leading White_Space, prefixed by the opening run as it appears in text[0..s) + \n when it starts inside an open fence. White_Space is the assemble.v1.json trim set.

Normalize headings: split on \n; a line whose body (one trailing \r set aside and put back afterwards) is "## " + one of headings, then one or more spaces or tabs, then —, – or -, then anything, becomes "## " + that heading. Every other line is unchanged: unknown headings, ### and deeper, no whitespace before the dash, a heading that is only a prefix of a longer word.

spanCases.note: tail = clamp(floor(0.25B), 4000, 48000) = 28800; walk back whole messages while they fit, then move the start forward to a user message.
The tail always keeps at least the latest complete turn.
The walk-back start u2 is inside the previous checkpoint; the next message a3 is an assistant, so the tail starts at u4.
Nothing after the previous checkpoint is a user message, so there is nothing to condense.
No user message: moving the start forward to the first user message reaches the end, so the tail is empty.
